scope: Developing-agent review of actual printed theorem types and explicit Challenge definitions, matched byte for byte to the official full statement audit. The retained 1056 proof statements/axiom lists and 136 definitions are identical to the previous reviewed output. This is not independent human review.
reviewed_aspects: The three preliminary lemmas identify exactly the monic endpoint-one binary polynomial family, cardinality 2^m, and uniform event count divided by 2^m.
Theorem 1.1 conjoins rational irreducibility tending to probability one with reducibility minus sqrt(2/(pi*n)) being O(1/n), in the same n-1 internal-bit model.
Theorem 1.2 quantifies one positive pair c,C before every n>=3 and uses that same pair in both the logarithmic-exponential factorization bound and square-root cyclotomic-degree bound.

The cyclotomic product is a finite list product of positive-order cyclotomic polynomials, with multiplicities and the empty product; the remainder is ordinarily irreducible over the integers and has no cyclotomic divisor.
Theorem 1.3 quantifies every n>=1 and bounds the genuine degree-n endpoint-one binary companion event by 8*(3/4)^floor((n-1)/4).

The companion is distinct from the sampled polynomial and its reciprocal, and its reciprocal product agrees coefficientwise modulo four; no companion or nonreciprocity hypothesis is added to the sampled polynomial.
All 17 Challenge definitions are necessary for the model or one of the three theorem events. The probability law is explicit and no definitions contain holes.
Natural-number division represents floors; logarithms and square roots are real; Big-O has a uniform eventual constant and degree-zero total extensions do not change asymptotics.
The full library retains the previously reviewed proof statements and selected mathematical scope; the new wrapper only combines two existing conclusions.
Phase retrieval remains excluded. This is an agent review, not independent human review.
